findings.message: oneLine replaces line-breaking and control characters but lets Unicode format characters through: bidi overrides and isolates (U+202A–U+202E, U+2066–U+2069) and zero-width characters (U+200B–U+200F, U+FEFF). Each log line stays one line, but these characters can change how it looks in a terminal or log viewer, for example by reversing the reference id or hiding part of the scope. Before 115, the allow-list removed them. Fix: add \p{Cf} to the character class, and add a test row with a U+202E in the scope.
findings.scenario: logError(`a${'\u202E'}di`, new Error('x')) → the line holds an RLO, and a viewer shows the text after it reversed. No caller passes untrusted text into the scope today, so this can't be shown in practice.
